headline: The US and South Korea are planning a 6.47-gigawatt gas power plant in South Texas to power a data centre.
score_reason: Pool score 6 kept: official releases from the US Commerce Department and NextEra Energy; the project is a plan and several claims are the project side's.
importance_line: It matters to South Texas and to the Texas grid, which would gain new power, but the jobs and water claims come from the project's own releases and the first stage is not due until 2029.
summary: FOX 7 Austin reports, citing releases from NextEra Energy, the US Department of Commerce and Related Digital, that a 6.47-gigawatt gas power plant is planned in Encinal, Texas, to power a 5 gigawatt data centre on an adjacent site, with the rest of the power going to the Texas grid. The first stage is expected online in 2029 and full capacity in 2032, and the project is part of the US-South Korea trade deal.
notes: FOX 7 Austin read in full; source is FOX 7 Austin, which states its information comes from releases. Score 6 kept. The pool's $22 billion headline figure is not in the text read and is not used. Project-side claims (jobs, water) are labelled as such.
